# Warrant

> Signed records of what a repository's work is, who accepted it and who objected, that any reader re-assesses under
> its own rules. This repository keeps its own work that way, in `.warrant/`.

To ask whether you may rely on something in this repository (a release, a goal, a claim, a pull request head), you
need no clone and no configuration:

    pip install --pre "warrant-graph>=3.0.0a10"                          # rely: 3.0.0a10 and later
    warrant-agent rely github.com/s0fractal/warrant "warrant-graph==3.0.0a10"

It answers RELY, RELY ON RECORDS, WAITING, NOT DONE, SUPERSEDED or DO NOT RELY, with who accepted it, what stands
against it, and whether external `anchor@1` witnesses still match the served store (`--anchor ADDRESS` to add your own).
The same command reads any repository that keeps a `.warrant/` store, e.g. `warrant-agent rely github.com/s0fractal/minds ba1c174a`.

## Repository map (where to look first)
- **Core protocol (~2,500 lines):** `warrant/{jcs,keys,records,shapes,store,engine,graph,anchor,verify}.py` (no imports from `warrant_agent/`, enforced by `tests/boundary_test.py`)
- **Agent & remote interface:** `warrant_agent/{rely,anchor,remote,api,mcp_server}.py`
- **Repository governance loop:** `warrant/{gate,review,claims,roadmap,board,drift}.py`
- **Protocol extensions:** `warrant/{delegate,pact,witness,dream,pulse}.py`

## Filing a counterexample or pull request (no permission needed)
- **Object to any record under your own key:** `warrant init --voices && warrant say RECORD_ID "why"`
- **Before opening a PR:** run `python3 tools/check_pr.py` (checks `warrant_verify.py` freshness, stale mutants in `tests/mutants.py`, and core boundary `B1` in <1s).
